standard_prerequisites.name: Images and direct sums of maps of quasi-coherent O_X-modules are quasi-coherent
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Schemes, Section labelled schemes-section-quasi-coherent (canonical Stacks tag 01LA); invoked at proof lines 465-468
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the two closure properties that make the constructed image sheaf G' quasi-coherent, and again makes the image of H -> G -> F quasi-coherent.

standard_prerequisites.name: A quasi-coherent O_X-submodule of a quasi-coherent O_X-module is a kernel of a map of quasi-coherent modules, hence itself quasi-coherent, and the set of quasi-coherent submodules contained in a fixed submodule is a set
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Background from the same chapter and from Schemes, Section schemes-section-quasi-coherent (canonical Stacks tag 01LA)
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the indexing set A of all quasi-coherent submodules contained in G available so that the direct sum over A can be formed.

core_obligations: Index the construction by the set of all quasi-coherent O_X-submodules G_a contained in the given submodule G, and form the map from the direct sum of the G_a to F (proof lines 459-464).

Show the image G' of that map is quasi-coherent, using that a direct sum of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent and that the image of a map of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent (proof lines 465-468).

Show G' is contained in G, so that it is a candidate, and conclude from the definition of G' as the image of all the candidates that it is the largest quasi-coherent O_X-module contained in G (proof lines 469-470).

Prove the universal property: for a quasi-coherent H and an O_X-module map alpha : H -> G, the image of the composite H -> G -> F is quasi-coherent as the image of a map of quasi-coherent sheaves, hence is contained in G', so alpha factors through G'; conversely every map into G' is one into G (proof lines 472-479).
proof_roadmap: Construct the candidate: the image of the direct sum of all quasi-coherent submodules contained in G, mapped to F (proof lines 459-464).
Check quasi-coherence of the direct sum and of the image, and that the result lies inside G, which gives largest-ness (proof lines 465-470).
Verify the displayed Hom-bijection by pushing a map H -> G into F and using quasi-coherence of the image (proof lines 472-479).
difficulty_reason: The statement asks for a quasi-coherent O_X-submodule G' of a given submodule G of a quasi-coherent F that corepresents the inclusion G -> F, i.e. Hom(H, G') = Hom(H, G) for every quasi-coherent H, and records that G' is the largest such (statement lines 445-455). The proof is a genuine construction rather than a citation: it takes the direct sum of all quasi-coherent submodules contained in G and defines G' as its image in F (proof lines 459-464), which requires knowing that direct sums and images of maps of quasi-coherent sheaves stay quasi-coherent (proof lines 465-468). The universal property is then proved by observing that for any alpha : H -> G the image of H -> G -> F is itself a quasi-coherent submodule of G, hence already a summand of the direct sum, hence contained in G' (proof lines 472-479). This is H2: one construction plus one short factoring argument, with no hypotheses on X beyond the definitions.
